title: Article lists default to 20 items with offset pagination and no upper limit.
content:
DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT is 20 and DEFAULT_ARTICLES_OFFSET is 0; limit is only constrained by ge=1 and offset by ge=0. A client can request any page size.
Source: app/app/models/schemas/articles.py:8

title: Bad or unknown tokens are answered with HTTP 403, not 401.
content:
_get_authorization_header raises HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN for a malformed header or wrong prefix, and _get_current_user raises 403 for an undecodable token or a username that no longer exists. Tests and clients may depend on this status code.
Source: app/app/api/dependencies/authentication.py:54

title: Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL.
content:
The articles.author_id foreign key uses ondelete="SET NULL", while comments, favorites and follows use CASCADE. Code reading an article must tolerate a missing author.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:108

title: Only the article author may update or delete it, checked by comparing usernames.
content:
check_user_can_modify_article compares article.author.username with the current user's username. check_article_modification_permissions raises 403 otherwise and is attached to the PUT and DELETE routes.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:23

title: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
content:
pwd_context uses schemes=["bcrypt"] with deprecated="auto", and get_password_hash and verify_password both go through it. Switching the scheme makes existing hashes unverifiable unless the old scheme stays in the list.
Source: app/app/services/security.py:4

title: All API models expose camelCase JSON names generated from snake_case fields.
content:
RWModel sets alias_generator = convert_field_to_camel_case and allow_population_by_field_name, and every schema inherits from it. Renaming a Python field silently renames the JSON key.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:21

title: Creating an article whose slug already exists is rejected with HTTP 400 instead of making the slug unique.
content:
create_new_article computes the slug and calls check_article_exists before inserting; if it exists it raises 400 ARTICLE_ALREADY_EXISTS. Two articles with titles that slugify alike cannot coexist, and the slug column is also UNIQUE in the schema.
Source: app/app/api/routes/articles/articles_resource.py:65

title: JWT access tokens are signed with the symmetric HS256 algorithm.
content:
create_jwt_token encodes with ALGORITHM and get_username_from_token decodes with algorithms=[ALGORITHM], so signing and verification both use one shared secret_key. Changing the algorithm breaks every issued token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:11

title: Access tokens expire one week after issue.
content:
ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES is 60 * 24 * 7 and create_access_token_for_user passes it as expires_delta, which sets the exp claim. There is no refresh token, so this value is the session length.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:12

title: The JWT payload identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
content:
create_access_token_for_user puts only JWTUser(username=...) into the token, and _get_current_user loads the user with get_user_by_username. A username change therefore invalidates older tokens, which is why the update route issues a new token.
Source: app/app/services/jwt.py:29

title: Database access uses named raw SQL files loaded by aiosql on asyncpg, not an ORM.
content:
queries is built with aiosql.from_path over the sql folder using the asyncpg driver, and repositories call queries.<name>. Dynamic filtering in filter_articles is built with pypika instead.
Source: app/app/db/queries/queries.py:5

title: A separate per-user salt column is prepended to the password before hashing.
content:
change_password stores a fresh bcrypt.gensalt() value in UserInDB.salt and hashes salt + password; check_password verifies salt + password. The salt column is NOT NULL in the users table, so both columns must be kept in step.
Source: app/app/models/domain/users.py:24

title: An article slug is derived from its title with slugify, and recomputed when the title changes.
content:
get_slug_for_article returns slugify(title). The update route calls it again when a new title is sent, so the article URL changes with the title.
Source: app/app/services/articles.py:19

title: Tags live in a shared table keyed by the tag text and are inserted with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
content:
The tags table has the tag text as primary key, and create-new-tags ignores conflicts so existing tags are reused. create_article calls create_tags_that_dont_exist before linking tags in the same transaction.
Source: app/app/db/queries/sql/tags.sql:9

title: The Authorization header must use the prefix "Token", not "Bearer".
content:
AppSettings sets jwt_token_prefix to "Token", and _get_authorization_header splits the header on one space and rejects any other prefix. Clients sending "Bearer <jwt>" are refused.
Source: app/app/core/settings/app.py:29

title: updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL trigger, not by application code.
content:
The migration creates update_updated_at_column() and BEFORE UPDATE triggers on users, articles and commentaries. Application updates do not set updated_at themselves.
Source: app/app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:27

title: Datetimes are serialized as UTC ISO 8601 strings ending in Z.
content:
convert_datetime_to_realworld forces tzinfo to UTC and replaces +00:00 with Z, and RWModel registers it as the datetime JSON encoder. It replaces the timezone rather than converting, so values must already be UTC.
Source: app/app/models/domain/rwmodel.py:7
